dataset.name: JaGOOD MVP Commodity Profiles
dataset.purpose: Provide commodity inputs for route-risk inference and scenario simulation.
dataset.preprocessing: temp_ideal_min_c, temp_ideal_max_c, and shelf_life_hours_at_ideal_temp were cross-checked on 2026-08-22 against public food-safety guidance (FDA, USDA FSIS, UC Davis Postharvest Research Center, IDFA); two values (Salmon Segar, Tuna Segar) were corrected to match the cited FDA fresh-fish guidance. delay_tolerance_hours and temp_sensitivity_level have no equivalent in public consumer/food-safety literature -- those sources describe safe storage duration under ideal refrigeration, not tolerance to in-transit temperature/time deviation, so these two fields remain internal MVP engineering estimates. Values are loaded without numerical transformation.
limitations: temp_ideal_min_c, temp_ideal_max_c, and shelf_life_hours_at_ideal_temp are grounded in cited public food-safety guidance, but that guidance targets consumer/commercial refrigeration safety, not cold-chain logistics specifically -- treat them as reasonable proxies, not regulatory transport standards.
delay_tolerance_hours and temp_sensitivity_level are not derivable from the cited sources and remain internal MVP judgment calls, not literature-backed values.

Values have not been validated against actual Indonesian cold-chain shipment outcomes; see app/services/historical_baseline.py and the shipment_records/corridor_baseline_stats tables for how real outcome data is (separately) collected going forward.
Shelf life and delay tolerance are simplified model inputs and must not be presented as guaranteed remaining product life or a food-safety certification.

sources.title: JaGOOD hackathon MVP commodity assumptions
sources.notes: Internal manually curated assumptions for commodity_type selection, delay_tolerance_hours, and temp_sensitivity_level -- fields with no public literature equivalent.

sources.title: Selecting and Serving Fresh and Frozen Seafood Safely
sources.notes: Fresh fish/seafood: store at 40F (4C) or below, use within 2 days of purchase. Applied to Salmon Segar, Udang Segar, Tuna Segar.

sources.title: Frozen seafood storage guidance (0F/-18C indefinite safety; 6-12 month best-quality window)
The Poultry Label Says "Fresh"
sources.publisher: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS)
sources.notes: Fresh raw poultry: 40F (4C) or below, use within 1-2 days. Applied to Ayam Segar.

sources.title: Ground Beef and Food Safety
sources.publisher: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS)
sources.notes: Whole-muscle fresh beef cuts: 3-5 days at 40F (4C) or below (ground beef only 1-2 days -- this dataset models whole-cut beef). Applied to Daging Sapi Segar.

sources.title: Pasteurized milk refrigeration guidance
sources.publisher: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) / U.S. Dairy
sources.notes: Ideal storage 34-38F (1-3C), FDA ceiling 45F; 5-7 days at or below 40F. Applied to Susu Segar.

sources.title: Spinach and Lettuce (Romaine and Loose-Leaf) produce facts sheets
sources.publisher: UC Davis Postharvest Research and Extension Center
sources.notes: Spinach/kale/chard: 3-5 days refrigerated (loose-leaf lettuce near 0C can last much longer, ~21 days -- this dataset conservatively models the faster-decaying leafy-green subtype). Applied to Sayuran Daun Segar.

sources.title: Tips on Storing & Handling Ice Cream
sources.notes: 0F (-18C) or colder; best quality 2-4 months. Applied to Es Krim.

sources.title: Guide to Minimize Food Safety Hazards of Fresh-cut Produce
sources.notes: Fresh-cut produce held at or below 41F (5C); shelf life 7-20 days across produce types, though the 7-day figure documented there is specifically for melons/tomatoes/leafy greens -- browning-prone cut fruit (e.g. mango, papaya) is not explicitly covered, so this dataset keeps a conservative shelf-life estimate rather than the upper end of that range. Applied to Buah Potong Segar.

commodity_type.method: Manually selected Indonesian commodity labels for the MVP; which commodities to cover is a product choice, not a literature-derived fact.

temp_ideal_min_c.method: Cross-checked against each commodity's cited public food-safety source; where the source gives a ceiling only (e.g. "40F or below"), the minimum retains its prior ice-storage-practice value since no source specifies a lower bound for unfrozen fresh product.

temp_ideal_max_c.method: Matched to each commodity's cited maximum safe refrigeration/freezer temperature; Salmon Segar and Tuna Segar were corrected from 2C to 4C on 2026-08-22 to match the FDA fresh-fish ceiling of 40F (4C).

shelf_life_hours_at_ideal_temp.method: Matched to each commodity's cited storage duration at ideal/safe refrigeration temperature; Salmon Segar and Tuna Segar were corrected from 72h/96h to 48h on 2026-08-22 to match the FDA fresh-fish guidance of 2 days. Used as a relative risk feature, not a food-safety guarantee.

delay_tolerance_hours.method: No public source found (as of 2026-08-22 research pass) that defines tolerance to in-transit temperature/time deviation specifically; public guidance covers safe storage duration under ideal refrigeration, not cold-chain delay tolerance. Manually defined operational threshold used by the synthetic label function.

temp_sensitivity_level.method: No public source found (as of 2026-08-22 research pass) that categorizes commodities into a Low/Medium/High transport temperature-sensitivity tier. Manually assigned category used by feature engineering.
